data.description:
## Description

**What**: Add a new `.github/workflows/review-sub-pr.yml` workflow that fires the existing LLM reviewer pipeline on PRs whose base ref matches `session/**`, `session-**`, `session_**`, or `bug-batch/**`. Coordinate the sub-PR merge trailer with S3's provenance grep so session→main provenance verification recognizes sub-PR-reviewed commits.

**Why**: After `per-branch-review.yml` was deleted, story PRs against session branches receive no internal LLM review. This story restores per-sub-PR review at the boundary where diffs are still small and reviewable. Without sub-PR review, the integration review at session→main cannot meaningfully skip and falls back to the full cumulative diff (which fails on 6000+ line PRs).

**Scope**:
- IN: `.github/workflows/review-sub-pr.yml` (new); coordination of sub-PR merge trailer grammar with `verify-session-provenance.sh:137`; two spike outcomes (filter base-ref semantics + SHA-based PR lookup reliability); manual `dso:code-reviewer-standard` (opus) review of this story's own sub-PR as a Definition of Done.
- OUT: Cycle ledger keying changes (S2); integration review skip logic (S3); RED-test-blocker required check (S4); version-bump shift (S5); worktree cleanup guards (S6); runner large-diff fallback (S7).

## Done Definitions

- When this story is complete, `.github/workflows/review-sub-pr.yml` exists and triggers on PRs whose BASE branch matches `session/**`, `session-**`, `session_**`, or `bug-batch/**` (verified by a `pull_request` event simulation or by an actual PR opening in the epic's own sprint).
  ← Satisfies: "Every per-story PR (sprint) and per-batch PR (debug-everything) triggers an internal LLM review via a new .github/workflows/review-sub-pr.yml workflow"

- When this story is complete, the sub-PR merge trailer grammar is coordinated with `verify-session-provenance.sh:137` so commits landing via a reviewed sub-PR are recognized as provenanced at session→main time. The chosen coordination is documented (either S1's sub-PR merge writes `DSO-Story-Merge:` OR `verify-session-provenance.sh` is extended to accept both `DSO-Story:` and `DSO-Story-Merge:`).
  ← Satisfies: SC1 + cross-story coordination per red team Finding #1

- When this story is complete, S1 spike outcomes are documented in the ticket comment thread: (i) the GitHub Actions `branches:` filter targets the PR's BASE branch (confirmed by a minimal test workflow); (ii) the `gh api repos/.../commits/<sha>/pulls` endpoint returns the expected open PR for a live pre-merge session-branch commit (or the 3rd-tier `gh pr list --search 'head:<branch>'` fallback is promoted to tier-1).
  ← Satisfies: "S1's spike validates the tier-2 reliability for pre-merge session-branch SHAs"

- When this story is complete, a manual `dso:code-reviewer-standard` review at OPUS model has been run against this story's own sub-PR diff. `reviewer-findings.json` is attached to the ticket as a comment, and zero unresolved critical/important findings remain at story close.
  ← Satisfies: "The first story (S1) is a hard blocker for all other stories AND its Definition of Done requires a manual dso:code-reviewer-standard (opus) review"

- When this story is complete, unit tests written and passing for all new or modified logic (workflow YAML lint, helper script unit tests).
  ← Satisfies: TDD Done-of-Done requirement

## Considerations

- [Reliability] In ci-pr mode, `merge-story-branch.sh` does NOT run for the local-to-session merge (per `dso-story-merge-trailer.md` contract — "trailer is NOT written to merge commits in ci-pr mode"). The trailer coordination decision MUST account for this: either GitHub's merge commit message must contain the trailer (via PR body propagation) or `verify-session-provenance.sh` must be extended to accept the linked-PR signal as equivalent provenance (already partially supported via lines 152-216).
- [Migration] When this workflow lands, in-flight sub-PRs created BEFORE its existence will not have been reviewed by it (the workflow only triggers on new pushes). Migration handling is owned by the cutover-migration story; this story documents the handoff but does not implement the migration.
- [Required-checks naming] If this workflow's check-context name will be added to branch protection as a REQUIRED status check (per SC5(a)), the addition MUST be staged after S1 lands (initially non-required), then promoted via the cutover-migration story. Otherwise every open sub-PR created before deploy becomes unmergeable.
- [Testing] The workflow MUST be exercised in this epic's own sprint as a load-bearing demonstration — the epic SC1 verification requires "the epic's own sprint demonstrates per-story sub-PR review firing." When the manual opus review runs against this very story's sub-PR, the workflow must already be functional.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a DSO operator, every per-story PR and per-batch PR gets an internal LLM review at the sub-PR boundary
